kinds.a: energy gel · sports gel · endurance gel · carbohydrate gel · energy chew · energy blok
kinds.d: Single-serve carbohydrate gel or chewable sweet taken during endurance exercise to keep up energy.

kinds.a: hydration drink mix · electrolyte powder · hydration tablets · electrolyte tabs · sports drink powder
kinds.d: Powder, sachet or effervescent tablet mixed into water to replace fluid, salts and sometimes carbohydrate during or after exercise.

brands.d: Berkeley, California maker best known for energy gels; founded by Bill Vaughan, who began developing a gel in 1990.
Seattle brand that pioneered low-sugar effervescent electrolyte tablets separate from carbohydrate; part of Nestlé Health Science.
British sports-nutrition company (SiS) known for isotonic energy gels, electrolyte drinks and hydration tablets.
Gothenburg sports-fuel company that introduced hydrogel-encapsulated carbohydrate drinks and gels in 2017.
Brand started by two British triathletes, making energy gels and ZERO electrolyte tablets.
Brand founded by triathlete Andy Blow around sweat testing and sodium-graded electrolyte products, later adding gels.
Durango, Colorado maker of Endurance Fuel, a drink mix supplying calories and electrolytes together.
El Segundo, California brand of electrolyte drink-mix sticks modelled on oral rehydration solution; acquired by Unilever in 2020.
Maker of fruit-flavoured sport hydration drink mix developed with Dr Allen Lim.

notes: Shelf rebuilt from 4 old kinds into 2. "Energy gels" (k40) became "Energy gel & chew"; its source is now the Wikipedia Energy gel article. The catch-all "Other electrolytes & energy products" (k37), "Hydration drink mixes" (k41) and "Hydration tablets" (k42) merged into "Electrolyte drink mix". Powder, sachet and tablet are now types ("t"), and the old source is kept. Brands added beyond GU and Nuun: SiS, Maurten, HIGH5, Precision Fuel & Hydration, Tailwind, Liquid I.V. and Skratch Labs. Clif Bloks stay as a model with no brand entry, because only a retailer page was retrieved. Dropped as SKU or lifestyle noise: Nuun Energy, Nuun Immunity and Nuun Vitamins as models (they are listed as Nuun lines in the brand register instead). Also dropped: the old ranges "GU Energy Gels" and "Nuun Hydration", which duplicated the models. Not added: ready-to-drink sports drinks (Gatorade, Powerade), which belong with Soft Drinks & Water; and pharmacy oral rehydration salts, which are a separate kind under Medicines. I found no independent test winner (Which?/CHOICE) for this shelf, so none is listed. Left blank where no retrieved page confirmed the fact: Maurten's founding year (the page only says hydrogel launched in 2017), the country of Precision Fuel & Hydration, and Skratch Labs' country and founding year.
